title: Letter to the ECB Joint Supervisory Team
description: A formal letter from a significant institution to its Joint Supervisory Team: sender, addressee, the letter, two signatories, enclosures, a copy to the national authority and an annex that lists every commitment with its owner and date.

facts.label: Legal name of the institution
facts.description: The supervised entity's registered name, as the ECB knows it.

facts.label: Postal address of the institution
facts.description: The registered office, on one line.

facts.label: JST Coordinator
facts.description: The full name of the head of the institution's Joint Supervisory Team at the ECB.

facts.label: JST Coordinator, as addressed
facts.description: How the letter addresses the JST Coordinator after "Dear".

facts.label: First signatory
facts.description: A member of the management body or another authorised signatory.

facts.label: First signatory's function
facts.description: The first signatory's function, as it appears under the signature.

facts.label: Second signatory
facts.description: The second authorised signatory, where the institution's signing rules require two.

facts.label: Second signatory's function
facts.description: The second signatory's function, as it appears under the signature.

facts.label: Contact for the JST
facts.description: Who answers the JST's questions on the letter: name, function and e-mail address.
facts.example: Alex Muster, Head of Regulatory Affairs (alex.muster@example-bank.eu)

facts.label: National competent authority
facts.description: The national authority that takes part in the institution's Joint Supervisory Team.

sections.heading: Sender
sections.guidance: The lines under the institution's name (the document's client) at the head of the first page: the address, and a telephone number or website if the letterhead carries them. Delete this section when the letter goes on the institution's own letterhead.

sections.heading: Addressee
sections.guidance: One line per address line. The ECB's postal address is Sonnemannstrasse 20, 60314 Frankfurt am Main. Check the JST Coordinator's name before every letter: coordinators rotate.

sections.heading: Letter
sections.content:
Dear {{fact:jst_coordinator_salutation}},

[TO DO: what this letter answers: the supervisory letter, decision or request, its reference and its date, and what it asked of the institution.]

[TO DO: the answer. One paragraph per point the JST raised, in the order it raised them. Say what has been done, with evidence the JST can check, and what will be done, by whom and by when.]

Each commitment this letter makes is listed in Annex 1 with the function accountable for it and its due date. {{fact:legal_entity_name}} will inform the Joint Supervisory Team without delay if any of these dates is at risk.

For any question on this letter, please contact {{fact:regulatory_contact}}.

Yours sincerely,
sections.guidance: The subject line is the document title: name the supervisory letter or decision being answered, with its reference. The heading of this section is not printed. A JST reads a letter for commitments: each one needs an owner and a date, and the annex is where the JST will track them. A [TO DO] blocks approval until it is replaced.

sections.heading: Signatories
sections.guidance: One row per signatory; each gets a signature line. Follow the institution's signing authorities; a letter that commits the management body is signed by its members.

sections.heading: Enclosures
sections.guidance: Every document sent with the letter, one per item, named as the JST will file it.

sections.heading: Copy to
sections.guidance: Delete this section when no copy goes to the national authority.

sections.heading: Annex 1: Commitments and due dates
sections.content:
| No. | Commitment | Accountable function | Due date | Evidence the JST will receive |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | [TO DO] | [TO DO] | [TO DO] | [TO DO] |
sections.guidance: One row per commitment made in the letter, numbered so later progress reports can refer to it. Interim dates are welcome: the ECB sets remediation paths with intermediate deadlines.
